title: CO-STAR: Conceptualisation of Stereotypes for Analysis and Reasoning
measurement_description: The paper measured the ability of language models to detect and generate implied stereotypes against various demographic groups, which included religious groups such as Muslims and Jews. The evaluation was based on a novel framework called CO-STAR, which involves conceptualizing the core idea of the stereotype.
findings: The paper's key finding is that its CO-STAR framework, which adds stereotype conceptualization annotations to training data, enables models to generate more accurate and context-specific implied stereotypes for various social groups, including religious ones. The models trained with this framework (CO-STAR-cs and CO-STAR-sc) generally outperformed ablated models and the previous state-of-the-art model (SBF-GPT2).
